claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately captures the prohibition on pilots taking off a U.S.-registered civil aircraft without briefing each person on board regarding safety belts and shoulder harnesses, including the Administrator authorization qualifier and balloon/airship exclusions.

The claim accurately reflects 14 CFR § 91.107(a)(2), prohibiting pilots from causing an aircraft to move on the surface, take off, or land unless passengers are notified to fasten safety belts and shoulder harnesses.

The claim faithfully conveys the general requirement under § 91.107(a)(3) that each person on board occupy an approved seat or berth with safety belt/shoulder harness secured during surface movement, takeoff, and landing.
The claim accurately reflects the exemption for dock personnel pushing off or mooring seaplanes or float-equipped rotorcraft during surface movement.
The claim properly reflects the permission under § 91.107(a)(3)(i) for an infant under two years old to be held by an adult occupying an approved seat without restraining devices.
The claim accurately captures § 91.107(a)(3)(ii) permitting persons engaged in sport parachuting to use the aircraft floor as a seat.
The claim correctly reflects the permission to occupy an approved child restraint system and incorporates the required accompanying attendant, labeling, and operator compliance qualifications.
The claim accurately states the labeling requirement for child restraint seats manufactured to U.S. standards between January 1, 1981, and February 25, 1985.
The claim captures the dual labeling requirement for child restraint systems manufactured to U.S. standards on or after February 26, 1985, including the red lettering requirement.
The claim accurately groups and represents all three alternative qualifying label standards under paragraph (a)(3)(iii)(B)(3) for seats not qualifying under (B)(1) or (B)(2).
The claim correctly captures the grandfathering provision allowing the AmSafe CARES device approved under former § 21.305(d) to continue bearing its FAA approval markings.
The claim accurately captures the rule that booster-type, vest- and harness-type, and lap held child restraints are not approved for use in aircraft, subject to noted exceptions.
The claim properly reflects the operator requirement under § 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(C)(1) that the restraint system must be secured to an approved forward-facing seat or berth.
The claim accurately states the operator requirement under § 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(C)(2) ensuring the child is properly secured and within the specified weight limit.
The claim accurately covers the operator requirement under § 91.107(a)(3)(iii)(C)(3) that the child restraint system bears the appropriate label(s).
The claim correctly reflects § 91.107(b)'s general exemption stating the section does not apply to operations under part 121, 125, or 135 unless otherwise stated.
The claim accurately conveys § 91.107(b)'s specific exemption providing that paragraph (a)(3) does not apply to persons subject to § 91.105.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 faithfully conveys all elements of U0000, including the pilot duty, briefing contents, and aircraft exemptions.
Claim C0001 fully preserves the prohibition and required passenger notification under § 91.107(a)(2).
Claim C0002 completely retains the general seating and safety belt requirement under § 91.107(a)(3).
Claim C0003 faithfully covers the seating and belt exception for seaplane and float-equipped rotorcraft dock mooring/push-off personnel.
Claim C0004 fully retains the permission, age threshold, and conditions for lap-held children under two years of age.
Claim C0005 completely retains the sport parachuting aircraft floor seating permission.
Claim C0006 fully captures the child restraint system occupancy permission along with accompanying adult requirements.
Claim C0007 covers the exact labeling requirement for child restraint systems manufactured between January 1, 1981, and February 25, 1985.
Claim C0008 fully covers the two-label requirement for child restraint systems manufactured on or after February 26, 1985.
Claim C0009 explicitly retains the alternative option for seats manufactured under United Nations standards.
Claim C0009 explicitly retains the alternative option for operator-furnished seats approved via TC or STC.
Claim C0009 explicitly retains the alternative option for child restraints approved under § 21.8(d) or TSO C-100b.
Claim C0010 completely captures the continuing labeling permission for the AmSafe CARES device.
Claim C0011 completely reflects the disapproval/prohibition for booster, vest-, harness-, and lap-held child restraints.
Claim C0012 fully covers the operator requirement that restraint systems be secured to approved forward-facing seats or berths.
Claim C0013 fully covers the operator requirement ensuring the child is secured within the restraint system's weight limit.
Claim C0014 fully covers the operator requirement ensuring the restraint system bears appropriate labels.
Claim C0015 faithfully captures the exemption for operations conducted under parts 121, 125, or 135.
Claim C0016 faithfully captures the exemption from paragraph (a)(3) for persons subject to § 91.105.
